key_insight: LogicEval provides a standardized, reproducible framework for measuring how well automated repair techniques handle logical (semantic) vulnerabilities in real-world software, exposing the need for semantics-aware approaches beyond traditional memory-focused APR methods.
problem_solved: There is no consistent way to evaluate and compare automated repair tools on logical vulnerabilities—bugs that arise from flawed program logic rather than memory errors—so practitioners lack benchmarks, metrics, and tooling to judge real-world repair effectiveness.
method: Curate a real-world dataset and taxonomy of logical vulnerabilities with ground-truth repairs to serve as a benchmark.

Define a reproducible evaluation pipeline and metrics (e.g., semantic correctness, functional/regression checks, security impact, precision/recall) to test classical APR and LLM-based repair approaches.
Support human-in-the-loop validation and standardized reporting so results are comparable, explainable, and actionable for tool developers.
impact: By standardizing datasets, metrics, and evaluation pipelines, LogicEval helps AI/ML practitioners identify which repair techniques actually fix semantics-driven bugs, accelerate development of more effective, semantics-aware models, and improve software security in production systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: dataset → taxonomy → repair tools (APR / LLM) → automated checks → human validation
Bar chart comparing repair success rates and false-positive rates across tool categories (classical APR vs. LLMs)
Matrix/heatmap of vulnerability types vs. repair effectiveness to highlight strengths and blind spots
Icon sequence: real-world bug → model suggestion → validated patch (emphasize semantic checks)
paper_title: LogicEval: A Systematic Framework for Evaluating Automated Repair Techniques for Logical Vulnerabilities in Real-World Software
paper_authors: Syed Md Mukit Rashid, Abdullah Al Ishtiaq, Kai Tu, Yilu Dong, Tianwei Wu
